scope: Provider-free follow-up. Full successful and partial receipt paths use an explicit synthetic oracle transport, not Jev inference.

checks.equivalent_command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=bench/jev python3 -B -m unittest test_adapter test_run test_bridge test_model_resolution test_audit test_complete_audit -v
checks.environment: Cleared inherited environment, only explicit safe paths, Git no-lazy-fetch/noninteractive settings, and known local evaluator binary.
new_checks: Complete exact-model synthetic campaign: 79 evaluations, 66 unique judgments, 68 occurrences, exact mixed label counts.
Mixed acceptance: 68 judged occurrences, 34 accepted, no replacement of abstentions with acceptance.
Complete synthetic alias-policy campaign retains the alias on wire and pins one declared test ID.
Semantic-stop projection preserves the wrong recorded label rather than substituting gold.
Actual adapter crossing at 1,200,000 reported tokens retains usage but excludes the crossing judgment from projection.
Erased, missing, falsy, and malformed transport metrics fail at named checks.
A forged completed over-budget body is rejected before eligibility or alias binding. Exactly 1,000,000 tokens remains eligible.
A real preflight credential-containment failure with zero transport calls needs no fabricated metrics.
Threshold and custody metadata contradictions are rejected.
Historical Git reads receive a minimal environment with lazy fetching disabled.

limitations: Synthetic transport controls do not validate TypeSafe compatibility, semantic quality, calibration, throughput, billing, or competitive advantage.

Replay checks local internal consistency and the default CLI resource envelope. It does not authenticate a provider, recover raw discarded bodies, reexecute historical implementations, or reconstruct the wall-clock deadline.
